newsitem.title: MEXICO: Fired attorney general says ran into obstacles.
newsitem.headline: Fired attorney general says ran into obstacles.

text.p: The recently fired former attorney general of Mexico, Antonio Lozano, said on Friday that in his two years at that post he faced "powerful interests" that impeded his work.
At a news conference Lozano acknowledged that the attorney general's office was marked by corruption, and that his attempts to overhaul the office were difficult.
"I had to confront negativity, inertia and resistance from powerful interests," he said.
In his first public statement since being pushed out of the job December 2, Lozano declined to speculate on the reasons why he was let go from his high-profile position.
Lozano was the only member of the opposition National Action Party in the government of President Ernesto Zedillo, of the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI).
"The reason will have to be given by those who took the steps," he said.
Government officials have said Lozano was let go because he was unable to produce results in several high-profile investigations into political crimes that shook Mexico in 1994.
In that year the PRI candidate in the 1994 presidental election, Luis Donaldo Colosio, was assassinated as was the secretary general of the same long-ruling party, Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu.
Lozano defended his work, saying he carried out his functions with loyalty and without fear.
"I was disloyal in front of no one and I showed fear before nothing," he said.
